quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When entering a curve, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
Where you can see and be seen best.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can see and be seen best.
questions.explanation: When entering a curve, position your motorcycle so you can see and be seen. On a left curve, ride on the right side to see oncoming traffic. On a right curve, ride left-center to see ahead without getting too close to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If you are towing a trailer on your motorcycle, your following distance should:
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more distance to stop.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do both at the same time.
Do one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull to the shoulder and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it first rains, roads become slippery. The center of the lane is especially slippery. Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles. The left tire track is usually safest.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind it.
Stop and wait until it starts moving.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change to a different lane to give it space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: In the center of a traffic lane, there is usually oil and grease buildup. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Find the lane with the least buildup.

questions.explanation: Avoid the oily strip in the center of the lane. It is usually narrow enough that you can stay to the left or right side and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: If you make eye contact with another driver, what does it mean?

options.text: It does not mean they will yield to you.
They will definitely yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact means a driver will yield. Drivers often look at motorcyclists but still fail to see them.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes occur?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times, even in daylight.

questions.question: Is eye protection required for motorcycle operators?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle operators are required to wear proper eye protection when riding.

questions.question: Your motorcycle starts to weave while riding over uneven metal bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Shift down to a lower gear right away.
Ride in a zigzag pattern until you cross the bridge.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves over uneven bridge gratings, stay calm and go straight across at a steady speed. Steering in a zigzag pattern is more dangerous than the weaving itself.

questions.question: When carrying a load on your motorcycle, where should it be secured?
questions.explanation: If not in saddlebags, loads should be secured as low as possible. Attaching a load to a sissy bar raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and can affect balance.

questions.question: You are wearing a protective jacket while riding in hot weather. What should you do?

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool.
Keep the jacket on for protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on for protection.
questions.explanation: A good riding jacket protects you in a crash, no matter the weather. Jackets also help prevent dehydration in hot weather. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to prevent overheating.

questions.question: The center of a lane has an oily strip. What does this mean?

options.text: It usually provides good traction unless it is raining.
Only ride on it if sharing the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It usually provides good traction unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip in the center of the road usually provides enough traction for safe riding, except when raining. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center lane.

questions.question: Your front wheel locks while braking. What should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
Release the front brake right away and use only the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake immediately and then apply it again.

questions.question: You and another vehicle approach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time. What should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to proceed.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Another vehicle is passing you from behind. Which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, how far behind the vehicle ahead should you ride?
questions.explanation: Maintain at least a two-second following distance under normal conditions. When conditions are not perfect, increase your following distance.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?
questions.explanation: To prevent collisions at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Be ready to change your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have more time to react to what other drivers do.
You have limited escape route options.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have limited escape route options.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react and room to move safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that traffic ahead is merging.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders be positioned?
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets more experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle in front of you so you can use its lights to see the road ahead.
Keep riding at your normal speed to reduce the chance of being hit from behind.
Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Slow down and increase your following distance so you have time to react to hazards.
